name: sec-preauth-s5-docs
title: Pre-auth S-5: docs and deploy notes for the bounded pre-auth slots, preemption/takeover and busy (docs only, verified against the code)
issue: DOCS-ONLY item (no code change): PR S-5 of C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/security-design-lua-editmode-and-preauth-slots.md PART 2 (read 2.1-2.8, especially 2.4 and the 2.6 line for S-5). The code is merged: S-1 #168 (Connection refactor), S-2 #171 (policy classes), S-3 #176 (acceptor + 4 workers + session thread, --preauth-slots, Busy plain Error, coalesced pre-auth logs), S-4 #177 (preemption by a strictly higher role, same-user takeover, no-token newest-takes-over, ErrorCoded busy = protocol 1.13.0, loopback backoff REMOVED in favour of a concurrency cap, TCP keepalive). FIRST audit what S-3 and S-4 already documented (grep docs/ for preauth, pre-auth, busy, takeover, slots, rate-limit, rate limit, Hello timeout, keepalive, proxy; read docs/editor.html, docs/logging-and-editor.html (anchor #rate-limit-gaps), docs/testing.html, any deploy/docker/linux docs pages, README flags tables) and write ONLY what is missing or stale. Expected gaps, each to be CONFIRMED against the code (EditorServer.cpp, Host.cpp, the pre-auth policy classes, the CLI/option parsing; never copy neighbouring docs): (1) the stale sentence 'a peer can hold the thread for the Hello timeout' (and any similar claim about one slow peer blocking the host) in logging-and-editor.html#rate-limit-gaps and anywhere else: replace with what is true now, and list the REMAINING gaps honestly (e.g. rate-limit gaps that still exist); (2) the flags/options: --preauth-slots (range, default) and any rate/handshake/keepalive knobs that exist: exact names, ranges, defaults, in the host command-line reference wherever flags are listed; (3) behaviour BEHIND A PROXY / port-forward / docker bridge / SSH tunnel: the host sees the proxy's address, so every client looks like one (often loopback) address and per-address limits and the loopback concurrency cap apply to everyone together; say what an operator should do (and what the code actually supports; do not invent a forwarded-for header feature); (4) the busy / preemption / takeover semantics from the operator and user point of view (who preempts whom, same-user takeover wait, what the client sees: ErrorCoded busy with holder role when the client asked for errorCodes, plain Error otherwise), and the protocol 1.13.0 note if the protocol doc is missing it; (5) deploy notes in the Linux/docker docs if they describe connection limits (container resource sizing: 4 workers + session thread + acceptor). Keep each addition short and factual; match the surrounding docs' style and structure (look at how other callouts and tables are written); update docs/index.html design-decision rows only if an existing convention says S-3/S-4 style changes get one and it is missing. Every sentence must be verified against CODE (this has cost many review rounds); where something could not be verified say nothing rather than guess. Docs-only: CI skips the build legs. If you find a real code bug while verifying, do NOT fix it: report it in dev.json notes/needsUser.
